blocks.hero.eyebrow: Anxiety counseling · Louisville, KY and online
blocks.hero.subhead: When anxious thoughts won't quiet down, you don't have to keep pushing through on your own. Counseling gives you practical tools, and someone in your corner.

facts.text: In person in Middletown or online

blocks.request.heading: You can feel steadier than this
blocks.request.text: Request an appointment in about a minute, or call (502) 523-2970. Most people are seen the same week.

signs.items.text: You can't turn your mind off, especially at night.
You're getting things done, but it feels like a full-time job just to hold it together.
Worry jumps from one thing to the next, and it's exhausting.
Your heart races or your chest tightens, and you're not sure why.
You avoid places or people because of how anxious they make you.
You've been told to "just relax," and it hasn't helped.

blocks.faith.heading: Faith at the center, never forced
blocks.faith.body: If you want faith to be part of how you work through anxiety, your counselor will bring it in. If not, you'll get the same excellent clinical care. You lead.

sections.heading: It doesn't have to make sense yet
sections.body: Anxiety can be hard to put into words. You don't need to have it figured out before you start. Early sessions are about building a clear picture of what's happening for you, and that's part of the work.

sections.heading: Practical tools, not just a place to talk
sections.body:
Counseling for anxiety at Freedom is active and practical. Our counselors use approaches with strong research behind them, including cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT), and mindfulness-based approaches. You'll learn what keeps anxiety going for you, and practice ways to respond that loosen its grip.

If unwanted, repeating thoughts are a big part of what you're facing, that may be OCD, which has a specific, effective treatment. See [OCD treatment](/ocd-treatment).

Your counselor tracks progress with you along the way, so you can both see what's helping.

sections.heading: Will I need medication?
sections.body: Not necessarily. Counseling alone helps many people. For others, medication from a physician works well alongside counseling. Your counselor can talk through what makes sense and refer you for a medication evaluation if it's worth exploring. Freedom doesn't prescribe medication.

sections.heading: When another kind of care fits better
sections.body: If your symptoms are severe and need psychiatric care or medication management, we'll help you find the right provider.

blocks.team.heading: Counselors who work with anxiety

team.items.text: Boys and men, age 8 and up, working through anxiety, worry, and panic.
Young adults and adults working through anxiety and perfectionism.
Women and older teens working through anxiety and shame.
Children, teens, and young adults working through anxiety and self-esteem.

blocks.expect.heading: Your first session
blocks.expect.body: It's normal to feel anxious about your first session. You'll talk about what you've been experiencing and what you'd like to be different, at whatever pace feels okay. Sessions are in our Middletown office or online.
blocks.cost.body: We don't bill insurance, but we'll give you a superbill to submit for possible out-of-network reimbursement.
